archetype.name: Pocket Passer (rhythm-and-vertical)
archetype.definition: An 11th-year timing passer who wins from the pocket by avoiding sacks and attacking 10+ yards downfield, with his legs used only to steal a first down or a short touchdown.

report.headline: Dak is the same top-12 passer; shootouts and soft defenses do the rest
report.take:
Strip away the record and Prescott in 2026 is almost exactly the quarterback he was in 2025. His 0.182 EPA per dropback ranks 12th, the same rank as last year's 0.191. His yards per game sit at 264.6, against 267.8 a year ago. His bad-throw rate is up, though, and his CPOE is down. What has changed is the setting around him. Dallas fields the 31st-ranked defense by EPA, so he has played a lot of high-total, back-and-forth games. Six of nine went over the total, and 37 attempts a game follow from that. That is why his yardage ranks sixth even though his efficiency ranks 12th.

The efficiency comes downfield. On throws of 10 or more air yards he produces 0.437 EPA per attempt, against 0.125 underneath. On 32 deep balls his CPOE is +7.9. Pickens (0.409 EPA per target) and Flournoy (0.381) have been the most efficient targets in the offense, with Lamb supplying the volume. The other pillar is sack avoidance. A 15.7% pressure-to-sack rate ranks third, and a 4.0% sack rate ranks eighth, well below the league's 7.3%. That is a big improvement on last year's 24.4% pressure-to-sack rate. The drag is the stuff behind the line: 57 screens and swings at -0.237 EPA, mostly to backs and the tight end, cost the offense real points.

The recent surge needs context. The last three games show 0.276 EPA per dropback, no interceptions and 6 TDs. They came against Philadelphia, Arizona and Indianapolis, whose defenses now rank 27th, 29th and 22nd. The two games before that came against Tampa Bay (2nd) and Green Bay (9th). He finished both with negative EPA and threw four interceptions, which is why his last-five rate is only 0.078. Over the hot stretch his CPOE was -1.7, so explosive plays were covering for spotty accuracy. His 14.3% bad-throw rate ranks 27th of 42 and is 3.1 points worse than last year. His 1.5% interception rate ranks 15th, which is kinder than his history: he ranked 49th of 63 in interceptions last year. Expect a few more picks. Four of his five have come on intermediate throws, and three over the middle, the one area of the field where he has been barely above zero.

The outlook from here depends on who is catching the ball. Pickens and Ferguson are both out, Turpin and Schoonmaker too, and the next opponent is a top-10 defense that rarely allows explosive passes. The volume should hold, because the defense guarantees it. Efficiency should settle toward his good-not-great baseline rather than the last three weeks.

strengths.title: Winning at 10+ air yards
strengths.body: Most of his value comes on throws beyond 10 air yards, where he averages 0.437 EPA, more than triple his underneath rate. His deep CPOE of +7.9 says the ball is landing in catchable spots, not just that receivers are bailing him out. The 32 deep attempts are a small sample, but his career aDOT and aggressiveness have been steady for years. The trait is real; the deep efficiency itself will likely cool.

strengths.title: Sack avoidance under pressure
strengths.body: He turns only 15.7% of pressures into sacks, third-best among qualifiers, and his 4.0% sack rate is far under the league average. His time to throw (2.79) is unchanged from last year, so this reflects decisiveness and protection rather than a quicker game. It is better than his own norm (24.4% last year). The last three games' 7.2% sack rate hints at some giveback, but the floor here is solid.

strengths.title: Shootout volume is built in
strengths.body: A defense ranked 31st in EPA keeps him throwing 37 times a game. His per-game yardage ranks sixth even though his efficiency ranks 12th. That is structural, not luck, and it should hold all season.

concerns.title: Accuracy has slipped beneath the production
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate has risen from 11.2% to 14.3%, and his CPOE is down, so explosive plays are hiding more misses than last year. Even during the strong three-game run his CPOE was negative. His 2023 and 2025 seasons show he can be cleaner. At 33 this is worth watching rather than writing off.

concerns.title: Good defenses expose the middle
concerns.body: Against Tampa Bay and Green Bay he produced negative EPA with four interceptions. His hot run came against three bottom-third defenses. Over the middle he averages just 0.059 EPA with three picks, and four of his five interceptions came on intermediate throws. His career interception ranks suggest the 1.5% rate will drift up.

concerns.title: Depleted pass-catching group
concerns.body: Pickens, his most efficient target per throw, is out with a hamstring, and Ferguson is out with a knee injury, with both backup tight ends and Turpin also sidelined. Ferguson's targets were actually unproductive, so that loss is mostly about depth. Losing Pickens removes a vertical threat that drives the downfield EPA. Until he returns, more falls on Lamb and Flournoy.

trend.note: Four efficient weeks to open, then a two-game crash against top-10 defenses, then a rebound against three weak ones. The swings track the quality of the opponent more than any change in him.

nextGame.headline: Shootout volume against a defense that takes away his deep shots
nextGame.body:
San Francisco's defense attacks his profile at its strength. It ranks third in explosive pass rate allowed and fifth in deep EPA, the areas where Prescott earns most of his value. It is also the league's best run defense, so Dallas will have little to lean on but his arm. The openings are underneath, where the 49ers rank only 20th in short EPA and he has been efficient. Their pass rush also seldom finishes sacks, which plays into his best trait. The 55.5 total and an offense that ranks first in passing EPA point to another game where Dallas has to keep scoring, so volume should be there even if efficiency is not.

Availability cuts both ways. Dallas is without Pickens, Ferguson, Schoonmaker and Turpin, with Mingo questionable, so Lamb and Flournoy carry the target load and a depth tight end fills in. San Francisco's two starting corners, Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir, are both day-to-day. If either sits, with Nate Hobbs still on IR, the coverage behind them gets thin quickly. Losing Gracen Halton for the year further dents a pass rush that already struggles to finish. The early forecast calls for gusts near 25 mph, but the retractable roof should make that moot.

keyMatchups.title: Deep game versus explosive-stingy defense
keyMatchups.body: His downfield efficiency meets a defense that rarely gives up chunk passes, and he is without his best vertical target in Pickens. Expect fewer shots to land and more of the work to shift to short throws, where this defense is merely average.

keyMatchups.title: Lamb against a soft WR1 profile
keyMatchups.body: Lead receivers have scored slightly above their averages against San Francisco, while second receivers have been held far under. With Pickens out, Lamb's already heavy target share should grow, and that is where the offense's yards are most likely to come.

keyMatchups.title: Status of the 49ers' corners
keyMatchups.body: Green and Lenoir play nearly every snap and are both questionable. Their availability decides whether this is a tough coverage test or a chance to pick on backups.

nextGame.watch: Whether Green and Lenoir suit up, and whether Prescott still wins on 10+ yard throws without Pickens.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is the safest part of the projection. A bottom-two defense will keep Dallas in high-scoring games, and he has started every week, so 250-plus yards with close to two touchdowns a game remains the expectation. The efficiency should settle near his 2025 level rather than the last three weeks. The schedule will not keep serving bottom-third defenses, his deep-ball accuracy on a small sample will cool, and a rising bad-throw rate means the interception count probably climbs from its current low pace.

The near-term dip comes from the injuries. Without Pickens and Ferguson the offense narrows to Lamb and Flournoy, which should compress his downfield value for a week or two. Once Pickens is back, a range of roughly 250 to 290 yards a game and around 1.5 to 2 touchdowns is the realistic middle, with the sack rate likely drifting up toward something more normal.
swingFactors: Whether the bad-throw rate settles back toward last year's level

confidence.note: His efficiency is stable across two seasons, but receiver injuries and an opponent-driven trend cloud the near term.
